messages:
Samira: Quick heads-up — SAST run for authsvc/feature/kms-rotate returned 12 findings (3 high, 6 medium, 3 low). Highs: 2 secret-detection hits in test fixtures, 1 possible insecure-deserialization path. Need to decide owners and whether to page oncall.

sast-bot: [Automated] SAST report uploaded: https://ci.redwood/internal/sast/1819001234 — summary: 12 findings (3 high, 6 med, 3 low). Tags: secret-detection, insecure-deser.

Jon: I can take the insecure-deser triage. Can someone paste the stack trace and minimal repro?

Priya: I can take the secret-detection ones. Likely false positives — test fixtures include a dummy key. We should capture evidence and add a suppression with justification + link to KMS usage docs so audit trail is clear.

Evan: FYI the env var was introduced by the test harness change last week. I'll open a PR to change harness to fetch test credentials from KMS mock instead of embedding inline. That should remove the scanner hits.

Marta: Proposed short runbook steps: 1) create issue in security/triage labelled `sast-review` 2) assign an owner within SLA 3) attach failing file + minimal repro 4) if FP, add suppression with evidence (`commit+grep` or CI artifact) 5) if high and production-exposed, page oncall and open an incident ticket.

Samira: Two quick questions: what SLA should we use for owner assignment, and who pages for high severity — security oncall or service oncall?

Priya: SLA idea: medium = 24h to assign, high = 6h to assign. Page sec-oncall for anything with RCE/insecure-deser or high-confidence credentials leak. For config-only leaks where keys are test fixtures, page service-oncall if it affects runtime configs.

Evan: I'll link the PR for the harness fix and add a KMS mock lib so CI can run without plaintext. ETA: today EOD.

Marta: I'll create the triage issue now and start the suppression workflow. Note: suppression requires audit evidence — use `securityctl suppress --evidence=<artifact>` or attach the CI log screenshot.

Jon: Attaching stack snippet for insecure-deser (minimal):
```
java.lang.ClassCastException: com.redwood.rpc.Payload -> insecure.deserialize at com.redwood.auth.Serializer.deserialize(Serializer.java:87)
```
This runs in the auth deserialization path when accepting legacy tokens. I can craft a unit test to reproduce.

Samira: Thanks — sounds good. Action items: Evan PR for harness/KMS mock, Priya handles suppression evidence and docs, Jon writes repro + patch for deserialization hardening, Marta files triage issue and will escalate if we hit production scope. I'll page sec-oncall if Jon's repro shows exploitable RCE.

sast-bot: Suppression created by Priya: https://internal.redwood/security/suppressions/56321 (evidence attached).
